name: Shabana Mahmood
role: UK Home Secretary (2025–present); Labour MP for Birmingham Ladywood since 2010; former Justice Secretary and Lord Chancellor
summary: As Home Secretary, Mahmood introduced tighter settlement rules and advocated controlled immigration and integration. She voted to renew the UK nuclear deterrent and against legalising assisted dying, and she has advocated a two-state settlement for Israel and Palestine.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Personally pursued additional prison capacity and a strengthened national policing programme while also expanding alternatives to imprisonment.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: In her constituent letter on West Bank sanctions she endorsed declaring the occupation unlawful and opposed moves to entrench it.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Her Commons settlement statement explicitly rejected assimilation and endorsed integration that allows communities to retain their distinctive cultures.

assisted-dying.rationale: She voted against the second reading of the September 2026 bill allowing eligible terminally ill adults to obtain assistance to end their lives.

civil-marriage.rationale: She voted for the third reading of legislation providing for same-sex couples to marry in civil ceremonies.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Defended independent judicial constraints on ministers and pledged to uphold the European Convention on Human Rights.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Said 'rights flow from our responsibilities to one another' and 'rights earned through responsibilities fulfilled'.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Insisted that nobody is below the law and justice must serve rich and poor alike; affirmed equal rights across faiths.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Rejected ethno-nationalism, saying it struggles to accept that 'someone who looks like me' can be English or British.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Voted for the final passage of legislation financing new nuclear power stations.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Her settlement rules require higher English (A-level standard for those on visas) as a condition for settling.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Moved a motion defending tax-credit support for low-paid working families and opposed cuts preceding higher wages.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: She voted to renew the United Kingdom’s independent nuclear deterrent.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Argued a patriotism that embraces those who 'have a faith like mine' as English or British and warned against ethno-nationalism that denies it.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: She voted to retain the United Kingdom’s nuclear deterrent by renewing Trident.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: In the 2015 Syria debate she reported voting for British military action in Libya, an intervention to protect civilians abroad.

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: She reported voting to authorise military action in Libya, where the British intervention was authorised to protect civilians.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Defended government income support for working families, extending its role beyond defense, justice and property protection.

open-borders.rationale: Said 'we can only be open to the world if we are able to determine who comes in and who must leave'.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Endorsed patriotism joining enduring national traditions with an ability to welcome change.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: She told the Commons that Britain would not introduce a blasphemy law.

reduce-immigration.rationale: As Home Secretary she is cutting net migration (reporting a fall of nearly 70%) and says 'migration levels are manageable' is a goal, with an end to uncontrolled migration.

religious-exemptions.rationale: She defended retaining the exemption for religious non-stun slaughter in Westminster Hall.

religious-nation.rationale: Defended Britain as a multifaith democracy and affirmed equal belonging for Muslims, Jews and people without faith.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: She told the Commons she wanted legal mechanisms that ensure hate speech is prosecuted and said she was reviewing the statutory threshold.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: She voted against advancing the bill that would allow minimum service levels during strikes.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Explicitly described the prison-capacity problem as mathematics rather than ideology and commissioned an evidence-led cross-party sentencing review.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Commons division at third reading records her voting for the bill legalising same-sex marriage.

separated-powers.rationale: Defended Parliament making law and independent judges interpreting and enforcing it, including when this frustrates ministers.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: She told the Commons that schools should teach inclusive, age-appropriate relationships and sex education.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: In her Spectator interview she described biological sex as immutable and its recognition as fundamental to how most women understand their existence.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Explicitly insisted nobody, including government, stands above the law.

surveillance-ok.rationale: She backed the Investigatory Powers Bill at third reading, authorising interception and other surveillance powers used to address national security threats including terrorism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: During the Finance Bill debate she argued for restoring the 50p top rate and criticised the distribution of the tax burden after the cut.

universal-healthcare.rationale: She voted for a Trade Bill clause protecting the UK’s ability to provide a comprehensive publicly funded health service free at the point of delivery.

notes:
Frontbench speeches (2010-15 Treasury and education briefs) and votes as a minister follow party and Government lines, so those answers are held at medium or low. She resigned from Corbyn's shadow Treasury team over economics,; the most recent clear statements are used. Her Spectator interview with Michael Gove and Times interviews were not opened.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 17 answers taken from it, 17 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; previous answers not consulted. Full active list and remaining nulls reviewed. Living person: no inference. Speeches, the full accessible Katy Balls interview, constituent correspondence and personally labelled committee answers were read alongside selected recorded divisions; vote collection was partial, not a complete career voting history. September committee reading covers the opening policing sections, not the full hearing. The 2025 Gove podcast description was accessible but its full interview was not, so its advertised subjects are not scored. Agency proposals, announcements and implemented policy are distinguished. Settlement consultation is not treated as an already enacted universal ten-year requirement. Police AI supports human assessment rather than transferring governmental decisions to algorithms; offender tagging does not itself establish an opinion on counterterrorism surveillance. Child safeguards do not establish a general adult pornography prohibition. Opposition to self-ID alone does not resolve the broader legal protection of transgender people; immutable biological sex is not an assertion that gender is wholly biological. Opposition to extending abortion time limits does not establish opposition to abortion in most cases; the Northern Ireland commissioning vote is too indirect to settle that broad wording here. Faith-guided personal conduct and religious participation do not establish scriptural civil law, divine political authority, church establishment or denominational parties. Palestinian statehood does not establish a distinctly Jewish-state doctrine; condemnation of ethnic cleansing is not silently relabelled a formal genocide recognition. The NHS motion title alone is insufficient to establish the precise universal-healthcare wording, and living-wage incentives are not automatically a substantial statutory minimum-wage increase. Means-tested asylum support does not establish that all social spending should replace universal provision. Border controls do not establish ethnic assimilation or minority expulsion. Ecology and technology searches and selected environment votes yielded no adequately specific position on the ecological statements. None of the ten listed Marxist, revolutionary or class-theory priorities was directly established; faith alone is insufficient to resolve the religion-illusion proposition. No inference is drawn from Labour membership or a social-conservative label.
